claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for child benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start by understanding your situation:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names (or you can use Child 1, Child 2, etc. if you prefer) and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. His name is Alex and he's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll now need to gather some more details to assess Alex's eligibility for child benefit.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex normally live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** (For example, school, college doing A-levels or similar qualifications, but not university degree courses)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 11, so he's just in primary school - regular school for his age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is there anyone else who might also be claiming child benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming child benefit for him. It's just me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital or care (such as local authority care) for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for a few months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for letting me know. This is an important factor. Let me ask you a few more questions about Alex's hospital stay:

**Are you continuing to contribute to the cost of supporting Alex while he's in hospital?** (For example, by providing clothing, paying for items he needs, or contributing financially to his care)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure to be honest. I mean, I visit him and bring him things sometimes, but I don't know if that counts as regularly spending money on him or not. It's been difficult.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - it's a difficult situation. Let me ask this to help clarify:

**Do you visit Alex regularly and bring him things he needs, or contribute in other ways to his support?** For example, do you bring him clothing, personal items, or other necessities on a regular basis?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do visit him, and I've brought him some things, but I'm honestly not sure if it's regular enough or counts as what you're asking about. It's been hard to know what to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is a difficult time for you. Let me ask one more specific question to help with the assessment:

**How long has Alex been in hospital - is it more or less than 12 weeks (about 3 months)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been more than 12 weeks - closer to about 4 months now, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing that information. Let me now read the official guidance to ensure I give you the most accurate assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Based on the information you've provided and the official guidance, I now need to understand one more important detail:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex?** This would include things like buying him clothing, personal items, food, presents, or other necessities on a regular basis - even if you're not certain it adds up to a specific amount.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Like I said before, I'm really not sure. I bring him things when I visit, but I don't know if it's regular enough or if it counts. It's been a confusing and difficult time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is a very difficult situation and it's understandable that you're unsure about these details.

Based on the information you've provided, let me make my assessment:

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 11 years old and in primary school, which meets the basic age requirement
- You live in the UK and Alex normally lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**The complicating factor:**
Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks. According to the official guidance, after 12 weeks in hospital, you would usually no longer be entitled to Child Benefit **unless** you regularly spend money on your child.

Since you're uncertain about whether the things you bring him when you visit count as "regularly spending money" in the way the rules require, I cannot definitively say whether you're eligible or not.

**What I recommend:**
You should contact HMRC (HM Revenue and Customs) directly to discuss your specific situation. They can assess whether your contributions and visits meet the requirements for the exception that allows Child Benefit to continue after 12 weeks in hospital. They will be able to look at your individual circumstances and give you a clear answer.

I hope Alex recovers soon, and I'm sorry you're going through this difficult time.
